test_title: PYST 25: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 20 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Identify the correct combination of the abbreviation, its full form and its application.

options.text: CD – Compact Disk – Used for high-speed internet access
ASCII – Automated Symbolic Code for Integrated Input – Converts images to code
ASCII – American Standard Code for Information Interchange – Encodes text in computers
LAN – Large Area Network – Used for connecting computers across continents

solution:
The correct answer is __**ASCII – American Standard Code for Information Interchange – Encodes text in computers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange)** is a character encoding standard used in computers and electronic devices to represent text.
 
• It uses **7 bits** to encode characters, supporting **128 unique characters**, including letters, numbers, punctuation marks, and control characters.
 
• ASCII is widely used in computer systems for **encoding and exchanging text-based data**, making it a fundamental element in the communication between systems and applications.
 
• This encoding standard is crucial for text data representation in programming, file systems, and communication protocols. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• Other options provided in the question include incorrect matches for abbreviations and their applications, as explained below.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **CD – Compact Disk:**

 
 
• A Compact Disk (CD) is a digital optical disc storage format introduced in the early 1980s.
 
• It is used to store and retrieve data, including audio, video, and computer files.
 
• However, a CD is not used for high-speed internet access, as mentioned in option 1, making the statement incorrect.
 
 
 
• **ASCII – Automated Symbolic Code for Integrated Input:**
 
 
• The abbreviation ASCII does not stand for Automated Symbolic Code for Integrated Input; this is incorrect.
 
• ASCII is associated with encoding text for computers, not converting images to code as stated in option 2.
 
 
 
• **LAN – Large Area Network:**
 
 
• LAN actually stands for **Local Area Network**, a network that connects computers within a limited geographical area, such as an office or home.
 
• It is not used for connecting computers across continents as mentioned in option 4. For such purposes, **Wide Area Networks (WANs)** are used. Therefore, this statement is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of ASCII:**
 
 
• ASCII has been integral in the evolution of computer systems, allowing machines to communicate using a standardized set of characters.
 
• It laid the foundation for more advanced encoding systems like **Unicode**, which supports a much larger set of characters, including those from various languages worldwide.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **ASCII’s Key Features:**

 
 
• Uses **7 bits**, allowing representation of **128 characters**.
 
• Includes **control characters** such as newline, tab, and backspace, in addition to printable characters.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of ASCII:**
 
 
• Limited to English characters, making it insufficient for global use.
 
• Led to the development of extended ASCII (8-bit) and later Unicode (16-bit or more).
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Used in programming languages for representing characters.
 
• Serves as a foundation for text-based communication in protocols like HTTP, FTP, and SMTP.
